floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 10 (build 42 vs 43) reconfirmed; 1-insn gap is a coupled RA load-delay NOP; no sibling analog; frontier = .greg dump + clean-target permuter.
Structural-reassociation axis KILLED with RTL proof: sched1 hoists the intrinsically-longer *arg0 reload chain above the partial-add, so no dataflow-preserving C form reaches {base->$a1, var_v0->$v0,

frontier.hypothesis: A directed/randomized permuter on a clean single-function target closes the coupled sched1/RA fixpoint that structural reassociation provably cannot.
frontier.mechanism: The target occupies a scheduler+allocator fixpoint {a2=$a2,base=$a1,var_v0=$v0,partial-first} that local dataflow-preserving transforms cannot reach (sched1 deterministically hoists the longer reload chain). A permuter search over structural mutations may find a non-obvious form that perturbs sched1's priority tie or register pressure into the target fixpoint.
frontier.next_probe: Build target.o from asm/funcs/ang_hosei_80056FE8.s + prelude at offset 0 (drop .set gp=64); run tools/permuter_campaign.py with --stop-on-zero + PERM_* directives seeded from the clean candidate; fresh-seed ~20-30 min windows, wait in-turn, harvest --stop before ending.

frontier.hypothesis: Preventing sched1 from hoisting the reload requires making the partial-add an illegal filler for the lh delay slot without changing dataflow.
frontier.mechanism: The 43rd nop survives only if no instruction independent of the lh result is available to fill its delay slot; the partial-add is that independent filler in every structural form. A form where the only remaining tail insn depends on the lookup would leave the slot empty.
frontier.next_probe: Investigate whether a sanctioned do-while(0)/LABEL_OUTSIDE_LOOP_P interaction or a reorg-level effect (NOT sched1) can suppress the delay-slot steal here; check .dbr dump behavior. Non-structural — needs the scheduling-technique catalog, likely a separate modality.
